advances: Fixed continuous normals and prescribed affine group sums. Free physical vertex stationarity requires an open feasible chart, and cap stationarity gives no global depth conclusion.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The map $x\mapsto (L_1(x),\ldots,L_m(x))$ is an affine isomorphism onto the hyperplane with coordinate sum one. If the thresholds in a group sum to at most one, some coordinate meets its threshold at every point. If their sum exceeds one, one can choose every coordinate strictly below its threshold while preserving sum one. This proves the exact cover region, which the motions preserve.

A proper trace of the reference homothet has volume $V_z(1-t_{giz})^d$ by similar simplices. Differentiation in its affine threshold gives the displayed $D_{giz}$ and the sign, while a strictly saturated trace stays of its type. To test threshold stationarity, assign any affine function to index $i$ and its negative to index $j$ in a group, with all other motions zero. Necessity of equal weighted moment vectors follows by testing every affine coordinate. Conversely their equality annihilates every allowed zero-sum tuple.

For physical velocities work in normalized barycentric coordinates of each reference fiber, so that its vertex matrix is $I$ and the thresholds are $t_{giz}$. Write $W=I+sB$ with zero column sums of $B$. In the proper open chamber the cap retains only its own vertex and has exact relative volume
$$
\frac{F_{gi}(W)}{V_z}=\det(W)\frac{(W_{ii}-t_{giz})^d}{\prod_{j\ne i}(W_{ii}-W_{ij})}.
$$
This is the product of its edge-length ratios times the simplex volume ratio, which is $\det W$ since column sums are one. At the reference its logarithmic derivative is $\operatorname{tr}B+\sum_{j\ne i}B_{ij}+d[(1-t_{giz})^{-1}-1]B_{ii}$. Full traces subtract the same volume derivative as the entire fiber, and empty traces subtract zero. Because $B_{jj}=-\sum_{i\ne j}B_{ij}$, the coefficient of the free entry $B_{ij}$ in the normalized Lagrangian derivative is
$$
-w_z+\sum_l e_{zl}-e_{zi}+\chi_{zj}.
$$
For $m\ge3$, comparing two row indices distinct from a third column index forces equality of all $e_{zi}$, and the vanishing coefficients then give $\chi_{zj}=w_z-de_z$. These conditions suffice as well. For $m=2$ the same coefficient directly gives $e_{zj}+\chi_{zj}=w_z$.

On one reference simplex the base-moment equation says $\kappa_g$ is independent of $i$. Write $K=\sum_g\kappa_g$ and $A_i=\sum_g\kappa_g a_{gi}$. Then $e_i=K-A_i$, $\chi_i=dA_i$ and $\sum_i A_i=K$. With $w=1$, for $d\ge2$ the equalities imply $dK=1$ and $A_i=K/m$, and these also imply all the equations. With $d=1$, $e_i+\chi_i=K$ directly, giving only $K=1$.
statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $m=d+1$, and $L_i$, $1\le i\le m$, be barycentric affine coordinates of a simplex $T$, with $\sum_i L_i=1$. At a finite set of sampled bases take reference fibers $K_z=c_z+r_zT$, $r_z>0$, of volumes $V_z$. Their labeled vertex evaluations are $b_{zi}+r_z\delta_{ij}$ in row $i$ and column $j$. For each group $g$, the caps $\{L_i(x)\ge a_{gi}(z)\}$ have affine thresholds in $z$ and fixed continuous normals. The allowed threshold motions $h_{gi}(z)$ are affine with $\sum_i h_{gi}=0$ identically. Each group's whole-plane cover region $\{\sum_i a_{gi}(z)\le1\}$ is preserved. Work in the open chamber with proper or strictly saturated traces and write, for a proper trace,
$$
t_{giz}=(a_{gi}(z)-b_{zi})/r_z,\qquad
D_{giz}=dV_z(1-t_{giz})^{d-1}/r_z,
$$
and $D_{giz}=0$ for saturated traces. Its global cap derivative in a threshold direction is $-\sum_z D_{giz}h_{gi}(z)$. With multipliers $\ell_{gi}\ge0$, threshold stationarity of total volume minus weighted cap masses is equivalent to
$$
\ell_{gi}\sum_z D_{giz}(1,z)=\nu_g\qquad\text{for every }i
$$
for a common vector $\nu_g$ per group.

When all physical vertex velocities are independently available on an open actual chart, set
$$
e_{zi}=\sum_{g:\,\mathrm{proper}}\ell_{gi}(1-t_{giz})^d,\qquad
\chi_{zi}=\sum_{g:\,\mathrm{proper}}d\ell_{gi}(1-t_{giz})^d[(1-t_{giz})^{-1}-1],
$$
and $w_z=1-\sum_{g,i:\,\mathrm{strictly\ full\ at}\ z}\ell_{gi}$. If $d\ge2$, the additional physical stationarity conditions are $e_{zi}=e_z$ independent of $i$ and $\chi_{zi}=w_z-de_z$ for all $i$. If $d=1$, these conditions are instead $e_{zi}+\chi_{zi}=w_z$ for each $i$.

For a single reference simplex with proper concurrent groups of normalized thresholds $a_{gi}$, the joint stationarity conditions for $d\ge2$ are that $\kappa_g=\ell_{gi}(1-a_{gi})^{d-1}$ be independent of $i$, $\sum_g\kappa_g=1/d$, and $\sum_g\kappa_g a_{gi}=1/(dm)$ for every $i$. When $d=1$ only the independence of $\kappa_g=\ell_{gi}$ from $i$ and $\sum_g\kappa_g=1$ are required.
title: Joint stationarity for affine motions of simplex cap group thresholds
